name: Atomic Content-Addressable Storage
description: Deduplicated content-addressable file storage with cas-public:// and cas-private:// stream wrappers, preserving full Drupal file entity semantics.
project_description:
Atomic CAS provides content-addressable storage for Drupal file entities. Instead of storing every uploaded file as a separate physical copy, the module hashes file contents with SHA-256 and stores the source bytes once per unique (hash, scheme) pair. Multiple file entities can reference the same underlying blob while preserving normal Drupal file semantics such as filenames, file entity IDs, and access control.

Features:

- Deduplicates source files by SHA-256 content hash; physical bytes are stored once.
- Provides cas-public:// and cas-private:// read-only virtual stream wrappers.
- Preserves Drupal file entity behavior with logical per-file URIs like cas-public://{fid}/{filename}.
- Serves public files through versioned, immutably cacheable URLs (/files/cas/{fid}/{short_hash}/{filename}); serves private files through the same route with hook_file_download() access control and no-cache headers.
- Optional Nginx X-Accel-Redirect and Apache X-Sendfile server acceleration.
- Deduplicates identical image-style derivatives for CAS-backed images via a shared hash-keyed derivative plus per-file symlink aliases.
- Provides Drush commands for migration, garbage collection, and blob auditing (with optional re-hash integrity check).

Blob storage roots are configured in settings.php (atomic_cas_public_root and atomic_cas_private_root), not in Drupal config. Both must be writable directories outside the document root. A hook_requirements() check surfaces missing or non-writable roots on the Status Report. An admin dashboard at /admin/reports/atomic-cas shows blob counts, deduplication ratio, space saved, and orphan counts.

This module is useful for media-heavy Drupal sites where the same file is uploaded multiple times, such as editorial, local government, publishing, and document-heavy platforms. Status: this project is currently a beta release intended for early adopters.
